import pandas as pd

# Load source tables with index_col=0 to ignore the first numeric index column
source0 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/intermediate_space/length6_31/training_0.csv", index_col=0)
source1 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/intermediate_space/length6_31/training_1.csv", index_col=0)
source2 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/intermediate_space/length6_31/training_2.csv", index_col=0)
source3 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/intermediate_space/length6_31/training_3.csv", index_col=0)
source4 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/intermediate_space/length6_31/training_4.csv", index_col=0)
source5 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/intermediate_space/length6_31/training_5.csv", index_col=0)
source6 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/intermediate_space/length6_31/training_6.csv", index_col=0)

# Step 1: Join Source6_31_4 and Source6_31_6 on 'batsman'
# source4 has ['batsman', 'no of balls', 'batsman_runs', 'strike']
# source6 has ['batsman', 'total_runs']
df_4_6 = pd.merge(source4, source6, on='batsman', how='outer', suffixes=('_x', '_y'))

# Step 2: Join Source6_31_0 and Source6_31_2 on 'batsman'
# source0: ['batsman', 'batsman_runs']
# source2: ['batsman', 'total_runs']
df_0_2 = pd.merge(source0, source2, on='batsman', how='outer', suffixes=('_x', '_y'))

# Step 3: Join Source6_31_1 and Source6_31_3 on 'batsman'
# Both have ['batsman', 'batsman_runs']
df_1_3 = pd.merge(source1, source3, on='batsman', how='outer', suffixes=('_x', '_y'))

# Step 4: Join Source6_31_5 and Source6_31_3 on 'batsman'
df_5_3 = pd.merge(source5, source3, on='batsman', how='outer', suffixes=('_x', '_y'))

# Step 5: Group by Source6_31_0.batsman with aggregations:
# avg(Source6_31_0.batsman_runs), sum(Source6_31_2.total_runs), avg(Source6_31_1.batsman_runs),
# avg(Source6_31_3.batsman_runs), sum(Source6_31_4.no of balls), sum(Source6_31_4.batsman_runs),
# avg(Source6_31_4.strike), sum(Source6_31_5.batsman_runs), sum(Source6_31_6.total_runs)

# To do this, we need to join all sources on 'batsman' first, then aggregate.

# Merge all sources on 'batsman' with outer joins to keep all batsmen
df_all = source0[['batsman', 'batsman_runs']].rename(columns={'batsman_runs': 'batsman_runs_0'})
df_all = df_all.merge(source2[['batsman', 'total_runs']].rename(columns={'total_runs': 'total_runs_2'}), on='batsman', how='outer')
df_all = df_all.merge(source1[['batsman', 'batsman_runs']].rename(columns={'batsman_runs': 'batsman_runs_1'}), on='batsman', how='outer')
df_all = df_all.merge(source3[['batsman', 'batsman_runs']].rename(columns={'batsman_runs': 'batsman_runs_3'}), on='batsman', how='outer')
df_all = df_all.merge(source4[['batsman', 'no of balls', 'batsman_runs', 'strike']], on='batsman', how='outer', suffixes=('', '_4'))
df_all = df_all.merge(source5[['batsman', 'batsman_runs']].rename(columns={'batsman_runs': 'batsman_runs_5'}), on='batsman', how='outer')
df_all = df_all.merge(source6[['batsman', 'total_runs']].rename(columns={'total_runs': 'total_runs_6'}), on='batsman', how='outer')

# Now perform the aggregations by batsman (group by batsman)
# Since each batsman appears once per source, aggregation is just to handle possible duplicates or NaNs

agg_df = df_all.groupby('batsman').agg({
    'batsman_runs_0': 'mean',      # avg(Source6_31_0.batsman_runs)
    'total_runs_2': 'sum',         # sum(Source6_31_2.total_runs)
    'batsman_runs_1': 'mean',      # avg(Source6_31_1.batsman_runs)
    'batsman_runs_3': 'mean',      # avg(Source6_31_3.batsman_runs)
    'no of balls': 'sum',          # sum(Source6_31_4.no of balls)
    'batsman_runs': 'sum',         # sum(Source6_31_4.batsman_runs)
    'strike': 'mean',              # avg(Source6_31_4.strike)
    'batsman_runs_5': 'sum',       # sum(Source6_31_5.batsman_runs)
    'total_runs_6': 'sum'          # sum(Source6_31_6.total_runs)
}).reset_index()

# Rename columns to match target schema:
# target schema: ['batsman': string, 'batsman_runs_x': float, 'total_runs_x': integer, 'total_runs_y': integer,
# 'batsman_runs_y': integer, 'batsman_runs_x_5': integer, 'no of balls': integer, 'batsman_runs_y_7': integer,
# 'strike': float, 'batsman_runs': integer]

# Map:
# batsman_runs_x       <- batsman_runs_0 (float)
# total_runs_x         <- total_runs_2 (int)
# total_runs_y         <- total_runs_6 (int)
# batsman_runs_y       <- batsman_runs_1 (float avg, but target expects int, so round)
# batsman_runs_x_5     <- batsman_runs_3 (float avg, but target expects int, so round)
# no of balls          <- no of balls (int)
# batsman_runs_y_7     <- batsman_runs_5 (int)
# strike               <- strike (float)
# batsman_runs         <- batsman_runs (sum from source4) (int)

# Convert types accordingly and fill NaNs with 0 or appropriate defaults

agg_df['batsman_runs_x'] = agg_df['batsman_runs_0'].astype(float)
agg_df['total_runs_x'] = agg_df['total_runs_2'].fillna(0).astype(int)
agg_df['total_runs_y'] = agg_df['total_runs_6'].fillna(0).astype(int)
agg_df['batsman_runs_y'] = agg_df['batsman_runs_1'].fillna(0).round().astype(int)
agg_df['batsman_runs_x_5'] = agg_df['batsman_runs_3'].fillna(0).round().astype(int)
agg_df['no of balls'] = agg_df['no of balls'].fillna(0).astype(int)
agg_df['batsman_runs_y_7'] = agg_df['batsman_runs_5'].fillna(0).astype(int)
agg_df['strike'] = agg_df['strike'].fillna(0).astype(float)
agg_df['batsman_runs'] = agg_df['batsman_runs'].fillna(0).astype(int)

# Select and order columns as per target schema
Target6_31 = agg_df[['batsman', 'batsman_runs_x', 'total_runs_x', 'total_runs_y', 'batsman_runs_y',
                     'batsman_runs_x_5', 'no of balls', 'batsman_runs_y_7', 'strike', 'batsman_runs']]

# Save to CSV
Target6_31.to_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length6_31/target_multisource.csv", index=False)

import pandas as pd

# Read sources with index_col=0 as per hint 21
s0 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length6_31/training_0.csv", index_col=0)
s1 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length6_31/training_1.csv", index_col=0)
s2 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length6_31/training_2.csv", index_col=0)
s3 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length6_31/training_3.csv", index_col=0)
s4 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length6_31/training_4.csv", index_col=0)
s5 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length6_31/training_5.csv", index_col=0)
s6 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length6_31/training_6.csv", index_col=0)

# Join Source6_31_4 and Source6_31_6 on batsman
join_0 = pd.merge(s4, s6, on="batsman", how="inner")

# Join Source6_31_0 and Source6_31_2 on batsman
join_1 = pd.merge(s0, s2, on="batsman", how="inner")

# Join Source6_31_1 and Source6_31_3 on batsman
join_2 = pd.merge(s1, s3, on="batsman", how="inner")

# Union Source6_31_0, Source6_31_1, Source6_31_3, Source6_31_5 (all have same schema: batsman, batsman_runs)
union_0 = pd.concat([s0, s1, s3, s5], ignore_index=True)

# Join union_0 and Source6_31_2 on batsman
join_3 = pd.merge(union_0, s2, on="batsman", how="inner")

# Join join_1 and join_2 on batsman
join_4 = pd.merge(join_1, join_2, on="batsman", how="inner")

# Join join_4 and join_0 on batsman to combine all
final_join = pd.merge(join_4, join_0, on="batsman", how="inner")

# Now group by batsman and aggregate as per target schema
# We need to produce columns:
# ['batsman': string, 
#  'batsman_runs_x': float, 
#  'total_runs_x': integer, 
#  'total_runs_y': integer, 
#  'batsman_runs_y': integer, 
#  'batsman_runs_x_5': integer, 
#  'no of balls': integer, 
#  'batsman_runs_y_7': integer, 
#  'strike': float, 
#  'batsman_runs': integer]

# Map columns from joined tables:
# join_1: s0 (batsman_runs) + s2 (total_runs)
# join_2: s1 (batsman_runs) + s3 (batsman_runs)
# join_0: s4 (no of balls, batsman_runs, strike) + s6 (total_runs)
# union_0: s0,s1,s3,s5 (batsman_runs)
# join_3: union_0 + s2 (total_runs)
# join_4: join_1 + join_2
# final_join: join_4 + join_0

# To avoid confusion, rename columns before aggregation:

# Rename columns in join_1
join_1 = join_1.rename(columns={
    "batsman_runs": "batsman_runs_x",
    "total_runs": "total_runs_x"
})

# Rename columns in join_2
join_2 = join_2.rename(columns={
    "batsman_runs_x": "batsman_runs_y",  # from s1
    "batsman_runs_y": "batsman_runs_y_7" # from s3
})
# But join_2 columns are s1.batsman_runs and s3.batsman_runs, both named batsman_runs
# So after merge, pandas will suffix _x and _y automatically
# Let's do the renaming after merge

# Actually, join_2 is merged s1 and s3, both have batsman_runs
# So after merge, columns are: batsman, batsman_runs_x (from s1), batsman_runs_y (from s3)
join_2 = join_2.rename(columns={
    "batsman_runs_x": "batsman_runs_y",
    "batsman_runs_y": "batsman_runs_y_7"
})

# Rename columns in join_0
join_0 = join_0.rename(columns={
    "batsman_runs_x": "batsman_runs_x_5",  # from s4.batsman_runs
    "total_runs": "total_runs_y"            # from s6.total_runs
})
# But join_0 columns after merge are: batsman, no of balls, batsman_runs (from s4), strike, total_runs (from s6)
# So rename batsman_runs to batsman_runs_x_5 and total_runs to total_runs_y
join_0 = join_0.rename(columns={
    "batsman_runs": "batsman_runs_x_5",
    "total_runs": "total_runs_y"
})

# Now join_4 = join_1 + join_2
join_4 = pd.merge(join_1, join_2, on="batsman", how="inner")

# final_join = join_4 + join_0
final_join = pd.merge(join_4, join_0, on="batsman", how="inner")

# union_0 has batsman, batsman_runs
# We want to sum batsman_runs from union_0 grouped by batsman as final batsman_runs
batsman_runs_sum = union_0.groupby("batsman", as_index=False)["batsman_runs"].sum()

# Merge batsman_runs_sum into final_join
final = pd.merge(final_join, batsman_runs_sum, on="batsman", how="inner")

# Now aggregate by batsman to get final output with correct aggregation functions
agg_df = final.groupby("batsman", as_index=False).agg({
    "batsman_runs_x": "mean",       # avg(Source6_31_0.batsman_runs)
    "total_runs_x": "sum",          # sum(Source6_31_2.total_runs)
    "total_runs_y": "sum",          # sum(Source6_31_6.total_runs)
    "batsman_runs_y": "sum",        # sum(Source6_31_1.batsman_runs)
    "batsman_runs_y_7": "sum",      # sum(Source6_31_3.batsman_runs)
    "batsman_runs_x_5": "sum",      # sum(Source6_31_4.batsman_runs)
    "no of balls": "sum",            # sum(Source6_31_4.no of balls)
    "strike": "mean",               # avg(Source6_31_4.strike)
    "batsman_runs": "sum"           # sum of unioned batsman_runs (s0,s1,s3,s5)
})

# Ensure column order as target schema
agg_df = agg_df[[
    "batsman",
    "batsman_runs_x",
    "total_runs_x",
    "total_runs_y",
    "batsman_runs_y",
    "batsman_runs_x_5",
    "no of balls",
    "batsman_runs_y_7",
    "strike",
    "batsman_runs"
]]

# Cast integer columns to int (where appropriate)
int_cols = ["total_runs_x", "total_runs_y", "batsman_runs_y", "batsman_runs_x_5", "no of balls", "batsman_runs_y_7", "batsman_runs"]
for col in int_cols:
    agg_df[col] = agg_df[col].round().astype(int)

# Write output
agg_df.to_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length6_31/target_multisource_critique_history.csv", index=False)
